cards.name: Marker-driven animation (expressions keyed to markers)
cards.summary: Fire an animation at every comp or layer marker: the expression finds the latest marker at or before the current time and animates from it, so moving a marker (a beat, a VO cue) moves the animation with no keyframes.
use_for: text pops on beats placed as markers
lower thirds in and out on VO cue markers
flashes or punch-ins on hits
cards.how: On Opacity (or Scale), with markers on the comp: var m = thisComp.marker, n = 0; if (m.numKeys > 0) { n = m.nearestKey(time).index; if (m.key(n).time > time) n--; } if (n == 0) value; else { var t = time - m.key(n).time; ease(t, 0, 0.3, 0, 100); }. Use thisLayer.marker for layer markers; m.key(n).comment carries a label (route different cues), m.key(n).duration a marker's length (hold until it ends).
cards.script_api: Expressions: thisComp.marker / thisLayer.marker (a Marker property): numKeys, key(index) (time order), key(name) (matches the comment; the earliest one on duplicates), nearestKey(t); MarkerKey .comment, .duration, .chapter, .url, .parameters, plus .time and .index. Script the markers: comp.markerProperty.setValueAtTime(t, new MarkerValue('cue')) (PVE 'Layer and composition markers').
cards.limits: nearestKey can return the NEXT marker, hence the index step back. With no markers numKeys is 0 and key() throws: keep the guard. Expressions re-evaluate every frame: long marker lists are fine, nested loops over them are slow.

cards.name: Live lines between layers: createPath() and points()
cards.summary: A shape path that is rebuilt every frame from layer positions: a connector between two nulls, a callout leader from a label to a point on a map, or a polyline through several points, with Trim Paths still working on it.
use_for: map connectors and route lines that follow animated pins
callout leaders that stay attached while things move
a graph line driven by sliders
cards.how: On a shape layer's Path: var a = thisComp.layer('A'), b = thisComp.layer('B'); var p1 = fromComp(a.toComp(a.anchorPoint)), p2 = fromComp(b.toComp(b.anchorPoint)); createPath([p1, p2], [], [], false). Read another path's vertices with thisComp.layer('Map').content('Route').content('Path 1').path.points(), or sample along it with pointOnPath(percentage) / tangentOnPath / normalOnPath.
cards.script_api: PathProperty.createPath(points, inTangents=[], outTangents=[], is_closed=true), points(t), inTangents(t), outTangents(t), isClosed(), pointOnPath(p, t), tangentOnPath(p, t), normalOnPath(p, t) (AE 15.0+). Set from a script with prop.expression = '...'.
cards.limits: Shape-path points are relative to the shape group's anchor (mask points to the layer's top-left), hence the toComp/fromComp round trip. Empty tangent arrays = straight segments. The vfx.py shape type cannot carry a path expression (its 'expr' covers transform, trim, fill and stroke only), so connectors are a hand or custom-script step.

cards.name: clamp(), linear() and ease() remaps
cards.summary: Keep a driven value inside limits (clamp) and remap one range onto another with linear or eased interpolation: the glue of every rig (a slider driving opacity, scale from audio amplitude, a counter that must stop at 100).
use_for: audio-reactive scale that never exceeds a cap
slider rigs with safe ranges
progress bars driven by a 0-1 control
cards.how: clamp(effect('Slider Control')('Slider'), 0, 100) on Opacity; linear(t, tMin, tMax, value1, value2) and ease(t, tMin, tMax, v1, v2) remap a driver (time, a slider, audio amplitude) into the output range and clamp at the ends; e.g. 100 + linear(thisComp.layer('Audio Amplitude').effect('Both Channels')('Slider'), 0, 30, 0, 25) on Scale (as [s, s]).
cards.script_api: clamp(value, limit1, limit2) works per component on arrays; linear/ease/easeIn/easeOut(t, [tMin, tMax,] v1, v2).
cards.limits: clamp on an array needs array limits of the same length. ease() is not the same curve as a keyframe's Easy Ease with custom influence.

cards.name: lookAt() and pointing layers at targets
cards.summary: Orient a 3D layer toward a target point (lookAt), or rotate a 2D layer toward one with atan2: arrows that point at a moving pin, a camera-facing card, a needle that tracks a value.
use_for: arrows and pointers aimed at map pins
3D cards that always face a target
gauge needles
cards.how: 3D: on Orientation: lookAt(position, thisComp.layer('Target').position). 2D: on Rotation: var d = thisComp.layer('Target').toComp([0, 0]) - toComp(anchorPoint); radiansToDegrees(Math.atan2(d[1], d[0])).
cards.script_api: lookAt(fromPoint, atPoint) (3D, returns an orientation); toComp/fromComp for 2D angles
cards.limits: lookAt returns an Orientation value: apply it to Orientation, not Rotation. Add a fixed offset if the artwork's 'forward' is not +X.

cards.name: Space transforms: toComp, fromComp, toWorld, fromWorld
cards.summary: Convert points between a layer's own space, the comp's 2D space and 3D world space: pin a 2D label to a point on a 3D layer, attach things to parented or scaled layers, or measure distances for focus pulls.
use_for: 2D labels and lower thirds that track a point on a 3D map
callouts attached to a parented, zooming layer
camera focus distance to a layer
cards.how: On a 2D label's Position: thisComp.layer('Map 3D').toComp([x, y, 0]); on a point inside another layer: fromComp(otherLayer.toComp(otherLayer.anchorPoint)); world-space position of a parented 3D layer: toWorld(anchorPoint). Direction vectors use toCompVec / fromCompVec / toWorldVec / fromWorldVec.
cards.script_api: toComp(point, t=time), fromComp(point, t), toWorld(point, t), fromWorld(point, t), the Vec variants, fromCompToSurface(point, t)
cards.limits: toComp on a 3D layer projects through the active camera, so the result changes when the camera moves (that is the point).

cards.name: Text style expressions (sourceText.style)
cards.summary: Drive font size, fill colour, font and the text itself from expressions (AE 17.0+), per character from 25.0: data-driven captions, a word coloured by a checkbox, size that adapts to a slider.
use_for: templates where a control changes the colour of one word
captions whose size follows a slider
counters that also change colour past a threshold
cards.how: On Source Text: text.sourceText.style.setFontSize(effect('Size')('Slider')).setFillColor([1, 0.82, 0]) (methods chain); setText(value) replaces the string; text.sourceText.getStyleAt(i, time) reads one character's style; per-character: setFillColor([r, g, b], startIndex, numOfCharacters) (25.0+).
cards.script_api: SourceText.style (17.0+): setFontSize, setFillColor([r, g, b] 0..1), setText, setFont, ...; getStyleAt(charIndex, t); createStyle(); per-character arguments 25.0+.
cards.limits: Colours are 0..1 arrays, not hex. Per-character arguments need 25.0+ (the installed AE is 26.0). Style expressions override the Character panel for those attributes, so a template user cannot then restyle them by hand.

cards.name: sampleImage() colour pickup
cards.summary: Read the average colour of an area of a layer at a given time: tint a graphic to the footage under it, drive a light wrap or glow colour from the plate, or detect brightness for auto-contrast text.
use_for: matching a graphic's colour to the shot
auto black/white caption colour from the background brightness
colour-reactive overlays
cards.how: On a Fill Color: thisComp.layer('Plate').sampleImage(thisComp.layer('Plate').fromComp([960, 900]), [60, 20], true, time); for caption contrast: var c = ...sampleImage(...); var l = 0.2126*c[0] + 0.7152*c[1] + 0.0722*c[2]; l > 0.5 ? [0, 0, 0, 1] : [1, 1, 1, 1].
cards.script_api: sampleImage(point, radius=[0.5, 0.5], postEffect=true, t=time) -> [r, g, b, a] averaged and alpha-weighted, point in the SAMPLED layer's space
cards.limits: Slow: it renders the sampled layer; keep the radius small and avoid it on many layers. The luma weights above are the Rec.709 coefficients applied to gamma-encoded values (an approximation).

cards.name: framesToTime() and timeToFrames()
cards.summary: Frame-exact maths in expressions: offset by whole frames regardless of comp rate, step animation to frames, or print a frame counter.
use_for: delays of N frames that survive a frame-rate change
stepped or held animation
timecode-like counters
cards.how: valueAtTime(time - framesToTime(3)) delays by 3 frames; timeToFrames(time) gives the current frame number; framesToTime(Math.floor(timeToFrames(time) / 2) * 2) holds every second frame (on twos).
cards.limits: timeToFrames adds the comp's display start time by default: pass isDuration=true or subtract it for durations.

cards.name: Index-based stagger and seeded randomness
cards.summary: Duplicate a layer and let each copy offset itself by its layer index (stagger) or pick a stable random value (seedRandom with timeless): cascades, scattered particles and varied-but-repeatable motion without keyframing each copy.
use_for: cascading bars or icons from one animated master
a grid of tiles that flip in one after another
random but frozen rotations or positions per copy
cards.how: Delay: var d = (index - 1) * 0.08; thisComp.layer(1).transform.scale.valueAtTime(time - d) on each copy's Scale (copy 1 = master). Stable random per copy: seedRandom(index, true); value + [random(-40, 40), random(-40, 40)].
cards.script_api: index (layer number in the comp); seedRandom(offset, timeless=false); random(min, max); valueAtTime(t)
cards.limits: index changes when layers are reordered or added above, which shifts every copy: reference a named master layer and keep copies contiguous. Without timeless=true, random() changes every frame.
